answer: One diver, one bed. The lagoon office leases a pearl oyster bed to a diver for a season, and every oyster opened is tallied against the lease. A ripple oyster prised from another bed fails the tally: at the ivory of the shell the growth rings must match the leased bed's own water, and a strange oyster tells of another lagoon. Buying a false lease means bribing the lagoon officer, forging a season of tallies and paying 19,700, and the wander stamp on the lease is checked at every landing, so a bed whose oysters were never counted is seized.
